title: The Proposal
text:
Minnetonka Stop at Six is a resident-led committee working to establish a 6% cap on annual increases in the City of Minnetonka’s property tax levy. Our goal is to help keep Minnetonka a great, affordable place to live through a budget initiative focused on the cap.

The Proposal
Your property tax bill shouldn’t be a surprise every year. We’re working to cap annual property tax levy increases at 6%, so Minnetonka stays affordable for the people who call it home. The property tax levy has nearly doubled over the last ten years. Has your income doubled?
Minnetonka works because of its people: families who’ve been here for generations, seniors who want to stay in the homes they’ve paid off, young families buying their first house, and small businesses on our corners.
When property taxes go up faster than paychecks and retirement incomes, those same people get squeezed out. Stop at Six sets a clear, simple limit. However, the budget changes; the levy can’t grow more than 6% in a year without a vote.

Predictable. Households and businesses can plan ahead.
Fair. Longtime residents and newcomers have the same protection.
Accountable. City leaders still have room to invest. They just must set priorities within a reasonable limit.

Legally, the Minnetonka Stop at Six proposal is a Minnetonka Charter Budget Amendment. It limits annual property tax levy increases to 6% - unless there is an approval vote from the residents.
You can find the current draft proposal language here


The Process
In order to get the proposal enacted requires a majority vote via a ballot initiative. The first step to getting an initiative on the ballot is to gather signatures. This is where we are at. The number of signatures is based on how many people voted in the Nov 3rd 2026 election. The plan is to have the initiative voted on in Nov 2027. This would mean that the property tax levy set in Dec 2028 (for tax year 2029) would be the first one implemented under the cap. This allows for the elevated property tax levy’s based on the current Public Safety Plan to be complete and Minnetonka returns to “normal”. In the future, the city would have an extra two percent plus to better Minnetonka on top of the normal cost of living.

title: Committee Changes
text:
On Oct 12th, the committee met to officially accept the addition of Kristin Gaarder and Tracy Ericksen to the committee.
With all 5 members present, Kelly Chermack was elected as President and Tom Stockert was elected as both Treasurer and Secretary.
The other item of business was a review of plans - including this website and petition timeline.

title: Committee Introduction
text: We are Minnetonka residents working together to support a 6% cap on annual City of Minnetonka property tax levy increases. We welcome residents who want to learn more, volunteer, or help with the initiative.

title: Committee Introduction
text:
Tom Stockert - Secretary / Treasurer
Tom Stockert moved to Minnetonka in 2013 and is a retired Chief Financial Officer and active local volunteer. He helped found a Minnetonka habitat restoration nonprofit, where he serves on the board and volunteers. He also volunteers with a local animal rescue and pursues other volunteer activities. Keeping Minnetonka a great, affordable place to live is a passion for Tom.

title: Committee Introduction
text:
Robert (Bob) Falk
Bob Falk has been a resident of Minnetonka for 37 years, retired business owner, former coach of youth sports. He has had many activities related to community service. He would like to continue to live in Minnetonka.

title: Committee Introduction
text:
Kristin Gaarder
Kristin Gaarder is a resident of Minnetonka, an active volunteer and board member with several local non-profit organizations focused on youth homelessness and outdoor recreation. She is committed to ensuring Minnetonka is an affordable vibrant community for all current and future residents.

title: Committee Introduction
text:
Tracy Ericksen
Tracy Ericksen has lived in Minnetonka since 2021 and is the founder of Kiwi Group, a Salesforce consulting business. She values the community and natural surroundings that make Minnetonka a special place to call home. She joined the committee to support responsible city spending and help ensure residents can afford to stay in the community they love.
